messages:
alex: Quick heads-up: customer on Dedicated hit failures when using our Python SDK from inside their corp network. Error was `ssl.SSLError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed`. They have an intercepting proxy and a company CA.

alex: Repro in their dockerized sample app:
```python
from redwood import Client
c = Client(base_url="https://dedicated.redwood.internal", api_key=TOKEN)
print(c.chat.create(message="hello"))
```

alex: They export HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY and set `SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors/company.crt` in the container. Curl + openssl ok, but SDK fails.

leah: What HTTP stack does the SDK use now? If it's httpx we default to `trust_env=False` which ignores REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE and proxy envs. If we use requests, env is used.

dan: We standardized on httpx a while back for unified sync/async. By default httpx.Client(trust_env=False) doesn't read env vars. I think the SDK constructor wasn't exposing trust_env or custom ssl.

alex: That explains why curl works and the SDK doesn't. Customer insisted on using the system CA file rather than bundling certs in the image.

ryan: Two angles: 1) quick fix - expose `trust_env: bool = True` and `ca_bundle: Optional[Union[str, ssl.SSLContext]]` on Client init; 2) long-term - add an examples directory and Dockerfile that shows copying the CA into a known path and setting env vars.

leah: For httpx, passing `verify=path_or_ssl_context` into `httpx.Client()` and `httpx.AsyncClient()` is the right approach. Also `trust_env=True` will let it pick up system proxy vars. We should also document differences between `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` vs `SSL_CERT_FILE` on various platforms.

dan: Typing note: make parameter `ca_bundle: Optional[Union[str, ssl.SSLContext]]`. Our stub files currently only accept str for `base_url` and `api_key`; need to update pyi/py.typed so editors don't show false negatives.

alex: There's another wrinkle: customer reported token lost after a 307 redirect through proxy (Authorization header removed). Our retry/redirect logic uses httpx's follow_redirects, and httpx by default removes Authorization on cross-host redirects. We should re-attach token for same-host or honor a client flag `preserve_auth_on_redirects`.

ryan: Good catch. Add an integration test: start a tiny proxy that issues 307 to a different host and assert auth header is present after redirect when flag enabled. CI can run mitmproxy or an nginx conf.

leah: Also ensure the AsyncClient path mirrors sync: i.e., `httpx.AsyncClient(verify=..., trust_env=...)`. I found our async wrapper forgot to pass `verify` through. That explains why some customers only see problems in async sample code.

dan: Proposed PR: add `trust_env` + `ca_bundle` args to public Client constructors, wire to httpx.Client/AsyncClient, update types, add two examples `examples/dedicated/httpx-proxy-sync.py` and `...-async.py`, and docs section `dedicated/proxy-and-ca.md`. I'll open it and tag for review. PR #3412.

alex: Workaround for customers now: run image with CA installed and set `SSL_CERT_FILE` and `trust_env` by manually constructing client like:
```python
import ssl, httpx
ctx = ssl.create_default_context(cafile="/etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors/company.crt")
client = httpx.Client(verify=ctx, trust_env=True)
```

ryan: CI bot: build-log: examples/dedicated image test passed when client manually sets `verify` (build 8812).

leah: Small DX suggestion: make the SDK surface a one-liner helper `Client.from_env()` that reads env vars and builds the right httpx.Client with `trust_env=True` and optional `ca_bundle` detection. Saves a lot of onboarding friction.

dan: Agree. I'll add `from_env` factory in the PR and a short sample Dockerfile to copy CA into `/usr/local/share/ca-certificates/` and run `update-ca-certificates`.

alex: Thanks all — customer unblocked for now. Keeping this open until PR merges and docs land. :white_check_mark:
